problem: A complete-listing filter excludes most products from a shopping study.

steps.answer: The rule requires observed price, description and features simultaneously.
The local snapshot contains missing fields; source omission, extraction, and availability timing are competing explanations.

root_cause: Verified exclusion mechanism: conjunction of three availability requirements. Origin of missingness is unresolved.
countermeasure: Report all-product and eligible-product results separately; audit missing fields against independently obtained source records.
reverse_check: Removing the filter restores eligibility by construction; improved fit or revenue must be tested separately.
confidence: High for exclusion mechanism; unknown for upstream origin.

problem: Most observed reviewers cannot support a multi-product history experiment.

steps.answer: Most user IDs have only one distinct reviewed product in this category snapshot.

steps.why: Why do they have only one?
steps.answer: Sparse reviewing, category restrictions and collection scope are possible explanations. Purchases outside the snapshot are unobserved.

root_cause: The snapshot lacks enough observed within-user history for most users; its behavioral origin is unresolved.
countermeasure: Begin with explicit context annotation; report the size and selection of any eligible history subset after temporal splitting.
reverse_check: More earlier reviews could enlarge eligibility; they would not establish that personalization improves customer fit.
confidence: High for data limitation; low for behavioral explanations.

problem: Opposing ratings cannot by themselves identify customer-specific product fit.

steps.answer: A single score does not identify the aspect, user need, product variant or reason for dissatisfaction.
Preferences, performance differences, variant mismatch, defects, shipping or authenticity concerns are rival hypotheses.
No adjudicated aspect/context labels or prospective shopper outcomes are available in this workflow.

root_cause: The desired construct (customer fit) has not been independently measured; there is no established cause of rating disagreement.
countermeasure: Annotate context, aspect, preference, defect, logistics and uncertainty with quoted spans; collect real shopper judgments before fit claims.
reverse_check: Better annotations may distinguish explanations; only held-out validation can show the distinction is reliable.
confidence: High for measurement gap; causal explanation unresolved.
